findings.title: Retain a GPU allocation path for native uncompressed streams without a processor

code_location.detail: Successful compatible native media type now returns without any allocator setup or processor insertion.

findings.preconditions: A native uncompressed video source supplies ordinary system-memory samples; the caller supplies a valid DXGI manager, explicitly selects the compatible native type, and the old allocator can initialize that supported format successfully. The transform list is empty. This does not require assuming that every D3D-manager source reader must return GPU samples.

source_proof.detail: Streams start with an empty transform list and the first native media type.
Selecting the existing native format returns S_OK before creating a transform. Matching another native type can also return S_OK at 1898-1913.
With no transform, the incoming source sample itself is queued.
The response now detaches without replacing its sample; synchronous return retains that exact sample at 1314-1327, and asynchronous delivery uses it at 1559-1563.
Before this patch every successful SetCurrentMediaType also ran reader allocator setup.
For video with a device manager that setup initialized an allocator with the manager even when no processor existed.
Before this patch a queued CPU sample was replaced with a newly allocated sample and copied before delivery.
The fixed allocator obtains ID3D11Device from a valid DXGI manager.
The successful allocation branch creates a texture and MFCreateDXGISurfaceBuffer, rather than returning the CPU input buffer.

findings.impact: This removes an existing source-level capability: a consumer of the previously returned DXGI surface now receives the source CPU buffer, which cannot provide that surface/shared texture. No processor exists to supply the proposed replacement allocator. This is a concrete representation regression relative to reader-original.c under the stated successful-allocation preconditions, not a claim of a measured game failure or a universal Windows API texture guarantee.
findings.requested_change: Keep or introduce a GPU allocation/upload path for native/CPU final outputs when a manager is supplied, while forwarding samples directly when the final transform already supplies the required GPU sample. A processor can be an alternative only if this native-compatible path actually inserts it.
findings.acceptance_gap: A bounded caller-owned native uncompressed CPU source plus DXGI manager must cover same-native-type selection, resulting buffer interfaces and texture sharing attributes, with and without an actual processor. Not executed by this review.

findings.title: Handle exhaustion of the now caller-retained processor sample pool

code_location.detail: Forwarding the processor sample transfers its finite allocator occupancy to the external caller instead of returning it after copying.

findings.preconditions: A final D3D-enabled canonical video processor is used, playback mode is off, the source can supply more frames, and a consumer retains all samples in that processor allocator while requesting another. The default reader minimum is 6 and this processor max is 10; a configured finite larger pool has the same boundary.

source_proof.detail: Reader supplies minimum output sample count 6 when the transform has not set one.
Processor initializes its own allocator with maximum max(count + 2, 10).
The PROVIDES_SAMPLES output path returns allocation failure directly, before consuming the pending frame.
An exhausted finite pool returns MF_E_SAMPLEALLOCATOR_EMPTY.
Pull failure other than NEED_MORE_INPUT is propagated; allocator exhaustion is not queued as a read result or deferred for retry.
On failed processing no next sample is requested; only a warning is emitted.
Media event handler clears SAMPLE_REQUESTED, records the processing error, but does not complete the pending read.
The event callback only warns on this error and rearms source events; it does not manufacture a read response.
Synchronous caller is waiting indefinitely on sample_event until a response/EOS arrives.

Returning an outstanding sample restores a free entry and optionally notifies allocator->callback. Neither inspected reader nor processor installs a retry notification callback. No read response or sample_event wake is generated here.
The old second allocator returned its own exhaustion error as a response while retaining the original queued sample. Its caller-held copies did not keep the processor output samples occupied.

findings.impact: The patch makes client retention exhaust the upstream processor pool. In a source that waits for explicit RequestSample, the failed read has no completion or scheduled retry; releasing a held sample alone does not resume it. The synchronous read can remain asleep, and an asynchronous request can lack its completion. This is a source-derived liveness defect under stated pool-pressure conditions; no hang was run or measured.
findings.requested_change: Provide bounded failure completion or a lifetime-safe allocator-release retry mechanism for MF_E_SAMPLEALLOCATOR_EMPTY before relying on the finite upstream pool for external sample ownership. Avoid busy retry while clients still hold every sample.
findings.acceptance_gap: Cover finite-pool retention through exhaustion, release from another thread, sync and async completion, and flush/release while a retry is pending. Not executed by this review.

checked_without_additional_findings.assessment: For successful outputs, queue_response AddRefs before the ProcessOutput local ref is released; sync ReadSample AddRefs before releasing the response; async callback receives a borrowed live sample until callback return. No introduced unbalanced ref was found in these paths.

refs.detail: Queue owns a reference.
Queue/push precedes local sample and event release.
Sync ownership transfer.
Async borrowed sample lifetime.

refs.detail: Processor uninitializes and releases its allocator.
Used sample entries are removed without releasing the live sample.

closure.detail: Actual ProcessOutput EMPTY marks the transform. process_sample now queues real error responses until admitted requests reach zero; each successfully queued response decrements requests once. closure.detail: The actual EMPTY is now returned before recursive drain can overwrite it. EOS queues errors rather than EOS for all remaining admitted requests. Already queued successful frames stay in front of these appended errors. Queue allocation failure exits rather than spinning.

closure.detail: A response already present when get_read_result begins prevents retry. A response queued during that retry does not have equivalent priority; see V3-P2-01.

findings.title: Recheck queued responses before returning an inline EOS retry error

code_location.detail: Failure returns before the newly queued response check.

findings.conditions: EOS, no response at entry, and a marked non-final transform whose retry emits at least one output before a later output attempt fails with EMPTY. This is a conditional multi-output/nested-transform case, not a claim about every final video-processor retry.
trace: source_reader_pull_transform_samples can successfully queue a final sample via the downstream transform, then continue pulling because next is non-NULL (949-974). A later output attempt can return EMPTY.
The queued sample remains live in reader->responses, but 1458-1465 immediately returns that later error and NULL sample. The response-presence check at 1467 is never reached.

The caller therefore receives a newer failure before an older successful response generated during the same retry. The frame is delayed until another read, contrary to the stated queued-response priority invariant.

refs.detail: A non-final pull may queue outputs and subsequently fail in the same call.
Only entry-time priority is enforced.

findings.requested_change: After the pull, prefer any response now queued for this stream before returning its later failure; retain the pending failure in a defined order if it still needs reporting.
findings.unexecuted_acceptance_case: EOS retry of a marked non-final MFT: one downstream success followed by true EMPTY in the same pull. Verify sample/error order for both synchronous and asynchronous APIs.

findings.origin: unchanged v2 prerequisite in current v3
findings.title: Propagated downstream exhaustion can still discard an unsubmitted source frame

code_location.detail: Only this transform's own ProcessOutput EMPTY marks it; downstream EMPTY leaves upstream pending output unmarked.

findings.conditions: A valid upstream transform A can retain multiple outputs per input, followed by finite-pool processor B. Pool pressure occurs again after one pending B output has been recovered. This does not require a broken transform contract.
trace: A emits output A1 successfully, then B accepts it but returns EMPTY. Only B is marked; A can still retain another output A2, while A.allocator_blocked is false.
The next read retries B, delivers its retained A1 and consumes the current request. source_reader_request_sample returns at 527-528, leaving A2 pending and A unmarked.
On a subsequent read no entry is marked, so the reader requests a fresh source sample S. In push_transform_samples(A,S), the pre-input pull at 801 tries to deliver A2 first.

If the consumer is again retaining the full B pool, B accepts A2 but returns EMPTY. push_transform_samples returns at 803 before ProcessInput(A,S). The source event handler still releases S at 1105, and no pending-input slot retains it.
Error completion avoids the old hang but cannot recover S, which A never consumed. This is a source-level frame/input loss path under the stated buffering and pressure conditions.

refs.detail: Pre-pull can fail before current source input is submitted.
Own flag cleared on successful A output; downstream failure does not mark A pending.
Unmarked upstream entries are skipped before obtaining another input.
Source sample is unconditionally released after processing returns.

findings.requested_change: Preserve pending upstream work across propagated downstream EMPTY, and do not request or discard a new source input before that work can be handled. Retain any source sample not yet accepted by ProcessInput if that state is still possible.
findings.unexecuted_acceptance_case: Two transforms, A emitting two outputs per source input, B with a caller-exhausted pool; recover one B output, re-exhaust, and account for every subsequent source input and output identity.

findings.origin: unchanged v2 flush prerequisite in current v3
findings.title: Canonical processor reports successful FLUSH without discarding its retained frame

code_location.detail: A success HRESULT clears allocator_blocked even though the inspected processor ignores FLUSH.

findings.conditions: The candidate uses the inspected canonical video processor, which retains a current_frame after allocator EMPTY. Flush is issued before that frame is recovered.
trace: The processor returns EMPTY before video_processor_process_output consumes current_frame (video_processor.c 1117-1122 versus 443-456).
Its ProcessMessage switch handles SET_D3D_MANAGER only; COMMAND_FLUSH enters the default branch, logs that it is ignored, and returns S_OK (1038-1065).
The reader drops queued responses and clears allocator_blocked after that S_OK, but no component discarded the pending processor frame.

After the caller releases a held sample, a later read can pre-pull that pre-flush frame before processing new input. Thus a success return and cleared reader flag do not establish the intended flush boundary.

refs.detail: Reader trusts successful transform FLUSH.
Reader removes responses, flushes transforms and clears request count.
Canonical processor ignores FLUSH.
Allocation failure preserves current frame.
Actual output consumption clears/moves current frame.

findings.requested_change: Close this precise processor FLUSH prerequisite, or provide another sound discard/reset path for its retained frame before clearing the retry state. Do not treat a no-op S_OK as evidence that the retained output was discarded.
findings.unexecuted_acceptance_case: Exhaust processor pool with a retained frame, flush, release a sample and read again; verify no pre-flush sample is returned. Confirm the exact linked processor identity before applying this canonical dependency conclusion.

limits: No build/link result, parent fixture or runtime report was audited. V1/v2/v3 run history is parent-reported; this review independently asserts no execution.

snapshot_binding.current_patch_binding: source-v5.json matches the current patch including mfreadwrite/Makefile.in. source-v4.json retains the prior patch digest 568c8bf2f2518c604c0d05345001ad4686ebeb83d6cebba5306627c2c26de798; that earlier digest is not misrepresented as current.

v3_closure.detail: EOS retry now checks for responses queued by the pull before returning a later pull failure. Existing responses also prevent entry into the retry. This closes the reported success-then-EMPTY ordering inversion.

refs.detail: Queued response priority both before and immediately after the retry pull.

v3_closure.detail: A successful producer remains output_pending even if forwarding to its downstream consumer then fails. The request helper repeatedly visits pending stages in reverse order before asking the source for new input, stopping on fulfilled requests or a real error rather than retrying EMPTY. Successful final output likewise remains pending until a subsequent NEED_MORE_INPUT probe. This preserves the upstream A2 pending state in the previously reported trace.

refs.detail: Own ProcessOutput success sets output_pending before the downstream call; downstream error cannot clear it.
Reverse probes precede any RequestSample; an actual error exits the loop.

v3_closure.detail: The provider now handles real COMMAND_FLUSH and discards current_frame, so the former ignored-S_OK path is removed. However unconditional unref loses the internally allocated fallback copy frame when it has been moved out of input_frame; see V4-P2-01.

refs.detail: New real FLUSH body.
Reader clears pending only on successful FLUSH.

findings.title: Preserve the reusable input copy frame when flushing a pending copied input

code_location.detail: Unconditional current_frame unref discards the allocation moved from input_frame.

findings.conditions: A supported input buffer cannot be wrapped with the required 16-byte alignment, so the existing copy fallback is used. The copied frame is still pending at Flush, for example after the output allocator returned EMPTY. The next input uses the same negotiated format and again requires the copy fallback.
source_trace: video_processor_init allocates the reusable input_frame once (549-552).
The alignment rejection at 235-239 selects the existing fallback at 419-422, which copies into input_frame and moves that frame into current_frame. av_frame_move_ref resets input_frame to defaults.
Normal successful output distinguishes the internal copy frame using !current_frame.opaque and moves it back into input_frame (453-456).

New FLUSH instead calls av_frame_unref(current_frame), releasing that internal allocation. input_frame is still the empty moved-from frame, and types/context are intentionally retained, so init is not rerun.

The next alignment-rejected input calls video_frame_copy_from_buffer on empty input_frame. It has NULL data, zero dimensions/strides and format -1; that helper does not allocate or reinitialize the destination. The subsequent move can therefore leave current_frame empty, causing output to report NEED_MORE_INPUT rather than delivering the valid next frame.

refs.detail: Wrapping rejects misaligned planes/strides/size before setting the external-buffer opaque marker.
Copy helper assumes a preallocated valid destination.
Copy fallback transfers the reusable frame.
Normal output explicitly recycles the internal frame.
Initial allocation of the reusable input frame.
Frame defaults clear storage and set format -1.
unref releases buffers; move_ref transfers and resets the source.
Image copy does not reconstruct an invalid-format destination.

findings.requested_change: When discarding a copied internal current frame, recycle its allocation back into input_frame as the existing output path does, or reinitialize and allocate a valid replacement before accepting another copy-fallback input. External wrapped frames should still release their borrowed buffer references, and caller-owned output samples must remain intact.
findings.unexecuted_acceptance: Use an input forcing the documented alignment fallback, retain it through output EMPTY, Flush, then feed another fallback input without renegotiating types. Account for both the reused internal storage and the post-flush output.

findings.title: Do not report success when allocating the error response fails

code_location.detail: Failed queue allocation breaks, then the helper unconditionally returns S_OK.

findings.conditions: A later synchronous read retries pending output; ProcessOutput again returns a real failure such as EMPTY; calloc for the first error response fails; no response was queued and no source request is in flight.
source_trace: queue_response returns E_OUTOFMEMORY at 477-478 before inserting a response or decrementing stream->requests.
The new helper breaks its response loop on that failure but discards the returned HRESULT and returns S_OK at 535. The analogous EOS completion loop at 546-549 has the same swallowing behavior.
The sync caller sees no SAMPLE_REQUESTED flag, breaks at 2633-2637, and because hr is S_OK calls get_read_result again.

With a non-EOS stream and an empty response queue, get_read_result sets status S_OK, sample NULL and stream_flags 0 and returns FALSE. The sync caller ignores that boolean in the post-loop call at 2642-2643 and returns the manufactured success. The admitted request count also remains outstanding.

refs.detail: Failure precedes queue insertion and response notification.
Both response-allocation failure branches are swallowed.
Empty non-EOS result resets status and flags to success.
Immediate no-source-request break followed by unconditional result consumption on successful hr.

findings.requested_change: Preserve and propagate the response-allocation failure when no queued completion can satisfy the read; keep queued-response priority if earlier completions exist. Ensure the corresponding admission is either completed or explicitly remains pending with a retry path, without reporting an empty successful synchronous result.
findings.unexecuted_acceptance: Fail the first error-response allocation during a pending-output retry and during EOS completion. Verify HRESULT/flags, absence of false S_OK, request accounting and bounded return; include a variant where an older successful response already exists.

additional_narrow_checks.result: No further finding in the normal successful-allocation path. EOS handler forwards drain failure to all existing requests. On successful drain it calls the pending-output helper; the helper emits EOS only after no output_pending stage remains, and its EOS branch cannot request another source frame. Completion loops decrement via existing response_ready and stop on queue allocation failure, avoiding EMPTY retry spins.

refs.detail: EOS drain and completion choice.
Probe loop, failure exit and explicit EOS branch.
One request decrement per successful response notification.

additional_narrow_checks.result: No source finding. The prepared Makefile adds only dxguid to existing IMPORTS. Reader now directly references IID_ID3D11Texture2D. The local Wine static library Makefile builds dx10guid.c, which includes initguid.h before d3d11_4.h; the local d3d11 IDL defines the texture interface UUID. This is the appropriate source dependency declaration for that new GUID reference; no new runtime spawner or codec policy is introduced.

refs.detail: Only static GUID dependency added to IMPORTS.
New external texture IID reference.
Static library source inventory includes dx10guid.c.
GUID instantiation precedes the D3D11 include.
Texture UUID declaration.

prior_finding_closure.detail: A pending copied internal current_frame (nonzero width and no external-wrap opaque marker) is moved back into the empty moved-from input_frame. A wrapped external frame is unreferenced instead. After the move current_frame is empty; repeating Flush takes the empty unref branch and leaves the recovered input allocation intact. Negotiated types/context and caller-held output samples are not modified by this delta.

refs.detail: Copy fallback moves reusable input storage into current_frame.
Existing normal-output recycling has the same ownership distinction.
New Flush uses width guard and returns copied storage before resetting the current slot.

prior_finding_closure.detail: Both request helper completion loops now return the actual queue allocation failure. On the reported single synchronous retry failure, the caller undoes its own increment, sets ERROR, keeps the failed HRESULT and skips the successful-result getter. The async no-queued-response non-EOS case also reports the native failure outside the lock. A separate response-reservation problem remains when another admitted read already owns a scheduled completion; see V6-P2-01.

refs.detail: queue_response failure is returned rather than swallowed.
Sync failure undo and FAILED(hr) prevent later S_OK overwrite.
Async undo and explicit native-HRESULT fallback.

findings.title: Do not consume a response already reserved by SAMPLE_READY after undoing the current admission

code_location.detail: Failure undo is followed by an inline pop through get_read_result, without transferring the older notification reservation.

findings.conditions: Multiple admitted async reads and the exact pending-output/response-allocation failure path being repaired. A queued GPU frame satisfies the direct-forward guard. Async work-item creation and submission succeed; the fault is response allocation, not notification submission.

concrete_source_schedule.action: Read R1 is admitted. Its source event reaches downstream EMPTY. Allocating its error response fails in process_sample at 1076-1078, leaving R1 admitted and the upstream/downstream output pending.
The caller frees one downstream pool slot and submits R2. The initial getter finds no queued response in this non-EOS stream; R2 increments requests at 1701.

concrete_source_schedule.state: requests = 1; one queued frame Q; one scheduled SAMPLE_READY
concrete_source_schedule.action: The pending-output helper recovers a frame Q into the newly freed slot. queue_response calls response_ready, which schedules SAMPLE_READY and decrements requests from 2 to 1. Q now supplies one of the earlier admitted completions.

With an upstream transform still holding another output, the helper continues because requests is nonzero. The downstream pool becomes EMPTY again; allocation of the next error response fails. The helper returns E_OUTOFMEMORY.

concrete_source_schedule.state: requests = 0; Q removed; SAMPLE_READY still scheduled
concrete_source_schedule.action: The new branch decrements requests at 1704, then get_read_result removes Q and reports it inline for the current READ command. No native failure callback is issued because report_sample is TRUE.

concrete_source_schedule.state: only one callback for two admitted reads; no remaining request count
concrete_source_schedule.action: The already scheduled SAMPLE_READY later finds no response at 1759 and emits no callback. One admitted read has disappeared from completion accounting. Releasing samples alone cannot complete it because requests is zero.

source_proof.detail: First response allocation failure can legitimately leave an older admitted request pending; the loop intentionally breaks.
Helper can queue an earlier success and continue pulling while one request remains, then return a later response allocation failure.
A successfully queued response schedules SAMPLE_READY and already consumes one admission.
get_read_result detaches/releases a response while retaining the sample for its inline callback.
Current admission is undone before consuming the response carrying the older reservation.
Only the inline successful-frame callback occurs for the current READ command.
An empty scheduled SAMPLE_READY emits no completion and restores no admission.

findings.impact: The new fallback can turn two accepted asynchronous reads into one callback and zero outstanding requests. This is a source-derived liveness/accounting defect in the explicitly retained-allocation-failure path, not an observed runtime hang. Sample AddRef/Release still balances; the missing ownership is an admitted completion.
findings.requested_change: Preserve notification/admission ownership when choosing an older queued response. Do not take a response already reserved by SAMPLE_READY as the current read's inline completion after cancelling that read's admission unless the displaced completion is also transferred or restored. Retain ordered native-failure reporting without falsely completing or dropping another admitted read.
findings.unexecuted_acceptance: Use two admitted async reads, fail R1's first error-response allocation, recover one valid direct-forward GPU output for R2's helper, then fail its next error-response allocation after a second downstream EMPTY. Drain all queued SAMPLE_READY work and assert exactly two completions or one explicit still-owned pending admission, with no zero-count lost read.

requested_EOS_check.result: No independently established reachable EOS masking defect in this delta; do not claim a hypothetical getter call is a demonstrated failure path.
requested_EOS_check.reason: The fallback calls the general getter, which can synthesize EOS when no queued response exists. However the same async READ command first calls that getter at 1698 under reader->cs. An already-EOS stream returns TRUE there and never enters the admission/helper/failure branch. In the inspected ordinary serialized path the lock remains held through the second getter, and the pending-output helper itself does not set stream->state to EOS. Thus the abstract possibility of the second getter returning synthesized EOS does not by itself prove this new native error is masked. A reentrant source/transform state transition was not established and is not assumed.

refs.detail: EOS pending-output errors are returned directly when no queued response takes priority.
Empty EOS getter synthesizes EOS and returns TRUE.
Initial getter, request admission, failure and second getter occur while the same critical section is held.
Callback occurs after leaving the critical section.

requested_EOS_check.unexecuted_acceptance: Keep explicit EOS plus allocation-failure coverage in the parent fixture; distinguish a concrete queued response from a synthesized EOS result if future control flow makes that fallback reachable at EOS.
